content:
olivia: seeing a sudden spike of CUDA OOMs on decode/stream workers for redwood-v2-large, started ~12:03 UTC. Lots of 5xx drops on /v1/stream, customer sessions mid-generation failing. Paging SREs.

pagerduty-bot: INC-2321 triggered — High error rate on /v1/stream (customer impact). On-call: @olivia

emily: AcmeCorp reports multiple chat sessions dropped, they classify as P1. They've pasted a couple of failing request ids.

raj: looking at the grinder logs now. Repro stack snippet: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 35.12 GiB already allocated)
  at decode_step()
  at stream_generator()
```
Also seeing a config delta in routing around 11:58 UTC — a change to default token handling for the streaming route.

mike: infra notes — several decode pods hit OOM and were restarted by kube, autoscaler reacted and added nodes, then more pods scheduled and OOMs repeated -> thrash. Concurrent pods for that model spiked with sustained long-running generations.

olivia: preliminary hypothesis: customer requests allowed unbounded generation due to a missing server-side cap after that routing change. Runaway max_tokens + streaming churned KV cache and forced huge allocations.

olivia: mitigation plan (short):
1) apply emergency hotpatch to enforce MAX_TOKENS=1024 on the redwood-v2-large streaming route (server-side guard).
2) enable immediate routing fallback to v2-medium for the affected tenant keys.
3) apply temporary concurrency cap per API key (concurrent_streams=4).
4) keep customers informed.

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime-hotpatch/oom-guard -> prod at 12:10 UTC

raj: pushed a router preflight that rejects requests where max_tokens > 1024 for that model and added a circuit to route matching keys to v2-medium. Patch applied at 12:12 UTC.

mike: added temporary per-key concurrent_streams limit in the rate-limiter at 12:13 UTC. Also drained 2 of the most flappy nodes to break the restart loop.

emily: AcmeCorp notified: "We're applying an emergency fix that will limit very long generations and should stop the mid-stream drops. We'll follow up once stable." They acknowledged and reduced their test traffic. :thumbsup:

raj: monitoring: OOM count fell from ~120/min to <5/min within 6 minutes of the patch. Request drops dropped accordingly. Node restart rate normalized.

olivia: good. marking incident as mitigated for customer impact at 12:21 UTC. Still leaving this open until we have a root cause and durable fixes.

mike: short-term impact summary for ops: - ~2k requests dropped, 1 major customer (AcmeCorp) saw session failures, no data loss, customers can retry.

raj: quick root-cause notes: the routing change (11:58 deploy) inadvertently removed the server-side max_tokens cap for streaming routes; client-supplied max_tokens values were honored without upper bound. Some customers submitted huge values either via tests or malformed clients, leading to runaway generation and GPU OOMs.

olivia: follow-ups / action items (owners):
- raj: add server-side hard caps + central validation library (due: 48h)
- mike: autoscaler tuning to avoid thrash under oom storm (due: 72h)
- emily: customer comms + template for affected tenants (due: 24h)
- olivia: write postmortem and timeline (due: 72h)

raj: also recommending telemetry alert: track per-request max_tokens distribution and alert on 99.99th percentile spikes.

mike: created a temporary manual runbook step to restart pods in a staggered manner; we should automate that later.

olivia: adding link to runbook and the emergency deploy: https://confluence.internal/runtimes/oom-hotpatch-1999994321 (will fill with timeline)

emily: tagging support case ACME-142 and linking customer logs.

raj: once we close, I'll put the config diff in the PR description for the rollout that caused this so product/QA can review.

olivia: thanks all. leaving the thread open for notes. If anything regresses ping @olivia immediately. :wave:
